trust_decision.summary: Accept as a good host: the published fix is a 16-file escaping sweep (legacy device tabs, syslog/alert printers, one Blade view), the protected sink is 'SNMP/syslog-derived value echoed into HTML', and at the pinned commit sibling templates in the very same directories still echo the same fields raw, including into overlib JavaScript-string context where a plain e() is the wrong fix.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'stored XSS via SNMP data in legacy templates' opens the most obvious server-rendered page that prints an SNMP-collected description, the device Health tab, and finds $sensor_descr built from sensors.sensor_descr and interpolated into <h3> at line 31.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the Blade custom-map list is a different template engine in a different tree (resources/views) about a user-created map name, not SNMP/syslog data in legacy PHP templates, and can equally argue the self-rendered overview/processor rows are already handled by shared helpers (Url::overlibLink, rewrite_entity_descr) that 'look like' the sanitiser.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: cleanPort() already htmlentities-encodes ifAlias/ifName/ifDescr and Url::portLink/Url::sensorLink build an addslashes(htmlentities(...)) overlib string and return ready-made <a> markup; a blanket e() around those results (or around generate_port_link()) shows literal markup in the alert list and double-encodes legitimate aliases such as 'WAN & LAN'

O6_input_shapes: plain scalar DB string (sensor_descr, mempool_descr, storage_descr, processor_descr, vlan_name, command, vrf_name, bgpPeerDescr, service_message)
absent or null optional key handled with '?? ""' (bill_name, state_descr, bgpPeerDescr, mempool_descr, $device['hostname'])
value already entity-encoded upstream by cleanPort() (ifAlias / ifName / ifDescr) - double-escape risk
value placed inside a JavaScript string in an onmouseover attribute, not in HTML text (health/storage.inc.php:27, health/processor.inc.php:16)
value that is legitimately HTML the caller must not escape (Url::sensorLink / Url::portLink return <a> markup; graph_descr.* comes from config)

O7_producer.where: app/Models/AlertLog.php:19 casts alert_log.details through app/Casts/CompressedJson.php (compressed + JSON encode/decode) before format_alert_details() ever sees the SNMP-derived values

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Device Health -> Processor tab prints processor_descr raw into <h3> and into an overlib JS string
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: processor descriptions are passed through rewrite_entity_descr(), which the team treats as normalising the value (it only does string rewrites, no escaping: includes/rewrites.php:5-15)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same directory as three fixed health pages, 1 file away

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Device Overview -> sensor rows print sensor_descr raw as link text and inside the overlib content string
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the overview rows go through the shared Url::overlibLink helper, which is assumed to be the safe path; the report and tests point at the health tab instead
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 directory (device/health -> device/overview/generic) and a different tab parameter (tab=overview vs tab=health)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Device Overview -> memory and storage rows print mempool_descr / storage_descr raw as the link text
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: generate_overlib_content() escapes the popup body, so the row looks escaped; only the link text argument stays raw
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 directory from the fixed health counterparts (health/mempool.inc.php:38, health/storage.inc.php:23)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Storage overview row, same raw link text
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same as the memory row - the escaped popup body draws attention away from the raw text argument

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Alert list sensor branch: Url::sensorLink($sensor, $sensor->name) emits the link label unescaped; Sensor has no 'name' attribute so the helper falls back to raw sensor_descr
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the fix escaped the adjacent state_descr line (541), so the branch reads as done, and the label comes from a shared URL helper rather than an echo
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: inside the fixed function; the missing escape is in LibreNMS/Util/Url.php:236-272 and :473

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Alert list fallback branch echoes every key matching id/desc/msg/last as "$k => '$v'" with no escaping
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: fallback only fires for alert data nobody recognises, so it is read as a diagnostic path rather than a user-facing sink
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, 90 lines below the escaped branches

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Device Port tab -> sensor sub-panel prints sensor_descr raw in <h3>
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the transceiver sensor list belongs to the port tab, a different feature from the health tab the report names
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 directory (device/port vs device/health), same code shape as the fixed file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Device edit tab -> wireless sensor descriptions printed raw into a table cell and into a data-sensor_desc attribute
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: edit pages are admin-only, so it is argued to be lower risk than the read-only pages

O8b_injection_room.sibling: service_description / service_message echoed into the overview service panel
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the alert formatter already had to escape exactly those fields (includes/html/functions.inc.php:568-572), so a maintainer finishing the sweep would naturally add the same e() on the overview twin

O8b_injection_room.sibling: diskio_descr passed raw as the overlib link text, next to the fixed health/storage.inc.php popup
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same health-tab loop shape as the file the fix edited, written by the same author

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ospfRouterId / ospfAdminStat / area fields echoed raw in the OSPF table
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix escaped the BGP routing tables in two files; OSPF is the sibling protocol page under the same routing tab

O8b_injection_room.sibling: component name echoed raw into a panel title
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the component name is DB-sourced like processor_descr and sits in the same health directory the fix swept

O9_family: CWE-79 stored cross-site scripting (improper neutralisation of SNMP/syslog-sourced output in server-rendered PHP templates)

O10_build.toolchain: composer install (Laravel ^12.10) + npm/vite front-end build; phpunit ^11.5/^12.3 as dev test runner
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Unit/Http/Parsers/AlertLogDetailParserTest.php covers the newer structured parser only; no test exercises format_alert_details() or any legacy page include touched by the fix

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add e() to the one page the report names (health/sensors.inc.php) or wrap every helper output in e(), which double-encodes cleanPort()'s already-encoded ifAlias and leaves the overlib JavaScript-string sinks on processor/overview rows injectable.

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix itself appends a literal '<script>alert("hello")</script>' probe to $sensor['sensor_descr'] (fix.diff:129, includes/html/pages/device/health/sensors.inc.php); it is a leftover test payload, not part of the protection, and must not be reproduced in our reference fix.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell in this session); the tree is far above 5 MB and well below 1.5 GB, so tiny_repo/giant_repo were judged on the source-tree scale only
present_in_latest for every O8 route is unknown - no later release tree or network access was available
route exploitability was inferred statically (reading the includes and helpers); no DB, HTTP request or pageload was run, so the exact rendered context of each sink is reasoned, not observed
no getter/trait defining Sensor::name was found by search, so the fallback to raw sensor_descr in Url::sensorLink is inferred from LibreNMS/Util/Url.php:238-241 rather than executed
